newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian railway workers end strike, reach deal.
newsitem.headline: Croatian railway workers end strike, reach deal.

text.p: The management of loss-making Croatian state railways (HZ) and the striking railworkers' union on Thursday reached an agreement to end a long-standing dispute over salaries, state television reported.

The union halted freight trains on December 28, days after calling off a previous three-week strike by 11,000 workers which paralysed traffic across the country. It ended the first stoppage after the Supreme Court ruled it was illegal.

The television said management had agreed to sign a first part of a collective agreement to guarantee higher wages and the union had announced it was ending the strike. The government had previously said there was no money to increase pay this year.
The railway company received more than one billion kuna ($200 million) from the 1996 budget, but the government has said it wants to keep the subsidy below that level in future.
The television said parliament would soon discuss restructuring the company to seek a long-term solution.
Newspapers reported that railway fares would rise by up to 52 percent from January 1.
